solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Duck energetic when meeting second bird

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like the letter O
to second a proposal is to back it

explanation.surface: A lively duck runs into a second bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a number qualifying the bird but is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive-back is a small African finch, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: God of love has narcotic drink prepared inside

indicators.note: inside says one word sits within the other, the drink wrapping around

parts.note: kava is a Pacific drink made from a pepper root, with a mild narcotic effect

explanation.surface: A love deity is served a narcotic brew that has been readied.
explanation.definitionFit: Kamadeva is the Hindu deity of desire and love, the counterpart of Cupid.

clue.text: It tastes gingery when served with a spirit

parts.note: as in the sense 'at the time that'
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Something tastes of ginger when mixed with a measure of spirits, like a ginger-and-rum cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive rather than a synonym: the plant's root has a ginger-like taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Asarum is the plant genus of wild ginger, whose root has a pungent flavour like ginger.

clue.text: Time for Christmas drink and children presenting poem

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated DEC
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
CH is the standard abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: A festive scene: Christmas, a drink and the kids performing a recitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A decastich is a poem of exactly ten lines, from the Greek for ten and line.

clue.text: Magistrate gets upset, being cut off

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means tipped over, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an aedile, also spelt edile, was a Roman magistrate

explanation.surface: An official is put out at being interrupted mid-speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To elide is to omit or suppress a sound or syllable, chopping it out of speech.

clue.text: Hat sitting on a cloak

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part sitting on another is placed above it

parts.note: a cap is a type of hat

explanation.surface: A hat perched on top of a cloak, as a costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A capa is a Spanish cloak or mantle.

clue.text: Wonderful perfume going off

explanation.surface: A lovely fragrance that is turning bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off' suggests a perfume being sprayed or fading, but here it means souring.
explanation.definitionFit: Acescent means turning sour, as milk or wine does when it spoils.

clue.text: Buffaloes very fearful, area being for termination of buffalo each time

indicators.note: one thing being for another means it stands in its place, swapping in
each time means the swap is made at every occurrence, not just once

parts.note: timorous means very nervous or afraid
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Nervous buffaloes in a jumbled field-guide description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Each time' means both Os in the timid word are replaced by A.
explanation.definitionFit: Timaraus, plural of timarau or tamarau, are small wild buffaloes of the Philippines.

clue.text: Chemical found in one small insect, not good

indicators.note: not tells us to take a letter out of the insect

parts.note: a midge is a tiny fly
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A chemical discovered inside a tiny bug, and not a pleasant one.
explanation.definitionFit: An imide is an organic compound with two acyl groups bonded to nitrogen, a chemical substance.

clue.text: Action of steersman taking vessel north

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase; the answer is the verb for that action

explanation.surface: A helmsman steers his ship northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, which fits the steering surface, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To cann, or con, is to direct a ship's steering, which is the helmsman's job.

clue.text: Sweep left something in the grate?

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
ash is what remains in a fireplace grate

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep has left behind something in the fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweep' looks like the chimney sweep of the surface but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash can mean to sweep or swish, as a tail or the waves do across something.

clue.text: The Parisian crook abandoning home of tears

indicators.note: the crook abandoning something means that part is left out of the word

parts.note: being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A French criminal leaves a house full of weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home of tears' reads as one phrase, but home belongs to the wordplay and 'of tears' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrimal is the anatomical adjective for things relating to weeping, as in the lacrimal glands.

clue.text: Porcelain one discovered by island wreck

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Fine china recovered near an island shipwreck.
explanation.walkthrough: The one is found beside the pair 'island wreck', which is written wreck first, then island.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is a Japanese porcelain ware, named after the port it was shipped from.

clue.text: Jolly types wearing a German coat in winter

indicators.note: something wearing a garment sits inside it, so one part is wrapped by the other

parts.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine; RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Royal Marines wearing a German overcoat on winter duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the white winter coat of the stoat, prized as fur.

clue.text: Drug vessel's keeping dry

indicators.note: the vessel has, and keeps hold of, the other word within it

explanation.surface: A drug container that has been kept dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Varidase is a trade name for an enzyme preparation used medically to break down clots, so a drug.

clue.text: Economist with leading principle, terribly insane

parts.note: a key is a guiding or central principle

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly disordered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An economist with a guiding idea that critics think is quite mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A Keynesian is a follower of John Maynard Keynes's economic theories, so an economist.

clue.text: African travels into volcanic hill

indicators.note: into places one word inside the other

parts.note: a cone is a hill built up by a volcano

explanation.surface: An African journeys up a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Congoese means a native of the Congo, an African person.

clue.text: Revolutionary fighter with servant under bridge

indicators.note: in a down entry, a part placed under another is written after it

parts.note: a valet is a personal servant

explanation.surface: A guerrilla and his servant shelter beneath a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests one over a river; here it is the bridge of a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevalet is the bridge of a bowed string instrument, which holds the strings up.

clue.text: Step taking country out of Europe finally

indicators.note: taking something away from a word removes it, so a letter is dropped
out of names the word from which the letter is removed
finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A political move to take a country out of the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: The first of the two Es is the one removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Grece, an old form of grise, is a step or flight of stairs.

clue.text: Indigenous Indian, hence displaced, longing for shelter

indicators.note: displaced means moved out of place, so the letters are rearranged
the rearranged word provides shelter, wrapping around the longing

explanation.surface: Native Americans driven from their land, longing for a place of refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheyenne are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Insect in booze? Pour out a different drink!

indicators.note: in places the insect inside the booze

explanation.surface: A fly has fallen in the beer, so tip it out and have something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be mother' is a British idiom for pouring the tea; tea is the different drink from the booze.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mother is the British idiom for taking charge of pouring tea for everyone.

clue.text: Grey adult, disinclined to communicate

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
shy people are reluctant to talk

explanation.surface: A grey-haired grown-up who keeps to themself.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy describes the pale greyish colour of ash.

clue.text: A very old name for a flower

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An antique name given to a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower in crosswords is often a river, something that flows; the Avon is the English river through Stratford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avon is a river, and a river is a flow-er in crossword convention.

clue.text: Soldiers certain to need knight for duelling contests

parts.note: soldiers are men in the ranks
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Troops are bound to require a knight for the jousts.
explanation.definitionFit: Mensuren is the German plural of Mensur, a ritual fencing duel among German student fraternities.

clue.text: Sticky young Aussie fellow kept outside group

indicators.note: one word kept outside another surrounds it

parts.note: in Australian slang a Roy is a trendy young man

explanation.surface: A young Australian left out of a clique finds things awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosety means resiny, from rosit, an old Scots word for resin, so sticky.

clue.text: What gets carried about by ship?

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what a ship transports.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the goods a ship or vehicle transports.

clue.text: A lot may change after end of war of course

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the other piece
end of picks the last letter of the word that follows
the letters may change their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Plenty may change once a war ends, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like a throwaway phrase but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotal relates to a rota, a regular course or round of duty.

clue.text: Sandy's drunk, getting scorn, as before

indicators.note: someone drunk is unsteady and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunken Sandy gets sneered at, as happened before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks the definition as an old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sdayn is Spenser's archaic spelling of disdain, meaning contempt.

clue.text: This writer's written about old city wall

indicators.note: written about means wrapped around the other word

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: An author has written about an ancient city's wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Mure is an archaic word for a wall, related to French mur.

clue.text: Boxes containing special ribbons

indicators.note: containing means holding the other part inside

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Gift boxes holding special ribbons.
explanation.definitionFit: Caddis is a worsted tape or binding ribbon, so caddises are ribbons.

clue.text: Grass left to grow up on island

indicators.note: in a down entry, growing up means rising from bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: rad is short for radical, a left-winger
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Grass abandoned to grow wild on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like abandoned but means politically left.
explanation.definitionFit: Dari is durra, a grain sorghum, which is a cereal grass.

clue.text: Jack and Jill reached this, turning up terribly late?

indicators.note: turning round makes the short word face the other way
terribly suggests disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The nursery rhyme pair arriving very late at their destination.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and Jill went up the hill to fetch a pail of water, so they reached a well.
explanation.definitionFit: A puteal is the stone curb or parapet round the mouth of a well.

clue.text: Arab wandering in a desert — no rest somehow

indicators.note: wandering things roam about, so the letters move out of order
somehow signals an unspecified way of rearranging
no means without, so the letters of that word are removed

explanation.surface: A nomad roams the desert with no chance to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the letters of rest from 'a desert' leaves three letters, which join 'in' for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adeni is a native of Aden in Yemen, so an Arab.

clue.text: Attempt to pen a novel, ending with utter rubbish

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, as in a pen

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: ending with picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An attempt to write a novel that ends up as complete garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashery is trash or worthless stuff, so rubbish.

clue.text: Vessel's partially wet, naturally

indicators.note: partially means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A boat is somewhat damp, as you would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, but it is a heating pot; not the volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: An etna is a small vessel for heating liquids over burning spirit.

clue.text: Monk strangely silent in church spoke finally

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so these letters are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A monk, unusually silent, finally speaks in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of spoke joins the anagram, and the whole sits between the letters of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A Celestine is a monk of the order founded by Pope Celestine V.
